description: GPU architecture capability matrix.  Each entry is the MINIMUM set of features a GPU must have for an engine's kernels to compile (or to dispatch correctly).  Used to decide which arch-specific code paths to add.

fields.name: Human-readable GPU name
fields.wave_size: Wavefront/warp size in threads (32 for NVIDIA/curry, 32/64 for AMD RDNA/CDNA, 32 for Intel)
fields.lds_kib: Local data share / shared memory per CU in KiB
fields.tensor_cores: bool: does this arch have tensor cores/MMA units
fields.wmma: bool: does this arch support Wave Matrix Multiply-Accumulate
fields.dot4: bool: does this arch have native int8 dot-product instruction
fields.dot8: bool: does this arch have native int8 dot-product-8 instruction

measured.provenance: RX 9070 XT (gfx1201), Windows, measured on-device; see PORTING-LESSONS.md sections 9, 12, 13

wmma_probed.note: ISA-verified by compiling and disassembling the unwrapped code object, not from a table
wmma_probed.spelling: gfx12 uses its own builtins with a _gfx12 suffix, eg __builtin_amdgcn_wmma_i32_16x16x16_iu4_w32_gfx12; gfx11 spellings and raw asm with gfx11 operand shapes are rejected
wmma_probed.operand_shape: iu4 16x16x16 takes one scalar int per lane (8 nibbles); iu4 16x16x32 takes a 2-wide int vector; iu8 16x16x16 takes a 2-wide int vector; f16/bf16 take a 4-wide vector; the accumulator is always 8 registers
wmma_probed.builtin_signature: integer matrix builtins take (A_sign, A, B_sign, B, C, clamp); confirmed from the compiler's own gfx12 CodeGenHIP test in the vendor source tree, not inferred from the manual
wmma_probed.modifiers: neg_lo:[A,B,C] carries the per-operand sign interpretation plus a trailing clamp flag; real signed-int8 tuned code emits 'neg_lo:[1,1,0] clamp'
wmma_probed.tuned_census: across the whole tuned GEMM set for this target: MatrixInstruction is always [16,16,16,1], MacroTile 128x128 is most common (then 64x64), DepthU is 32 or 64, and there is no 4-bit kernel in the set
wmma_probed.tuned_inner_loop: a real tuned int8 kernel marshals operands with a byte permute (V_PERM_B32) and a half-word shared-memory load (DS_LOAD_U16_D16 / _HI), pipelines with S_WAIT_LOADCNT, uses S_BARRIER_SIGNAL in the loop, and the compiler emits dual-issued pairs (V_DUAL_MOV_B32) in the same block
wmma_probed.operand_expansion: narrow packed weights can be widened to 4-bit operands in registers with a byte permute, so no expanded weight copy needs to exist in device memory: this is the difference between losing the context to the weight expansion and keeping it
wmma_probed.dtype_pairs: gfx12 matrix pairs, all same-type: fp16/fp16, bf16/bf16, int8/int8 -> int32, and fp8/bf8 in all four mixes, all at K=16; plus packed-int4/packed-int4 -> int32 at K=16 and K=32. There is no mixed fp16xint4 pair on gfx12, so an int4 weight operand forces an int4 activation operand. fp4, fp6 and mixed fp16xint4 exist only on the gfx1250 family
wmma_probed.int4_packing: the packed 4-bit operand type is two int4 per byte with the low nibble first, and a compile-time variant swaps the nibble order
wmma_probed.generator_gap: the assembly-generating path behind the vendor BLAS library does have 4-bit datatypes, but only 4-bit FLOAT, plus a packed 4xint8 dword type that is used for dot products and is not a 4-bit integer. Its 4-bit-float matrix path is gated to the later gfx1250 family, and this target's matrix instruction set has no 4-bit float opcode at all, so no 4-bit kernel is generatable from its solution yaml for this target. It has no 4-bit integer datatype for any target. The 4-bit integer matrix path lives instead in the vendor's kernel-template library, which does expose it for this target at K=16 and K=32. Practical rule: presence of a datatype in the generator's enum is not availability on your target, because the matrix opcode behind it is capability-gated per ISA
wmma_probed.fp8: exists only as WMMA; no scalar fp8 conversion (v_cvt_pk_fp8_f32 is rejected)
wmma_probed.pipeline_rules: ISA 7.12.1 needs >=1 independent VALU between WMMAs whose operands overlap the previous D; 7.12.2 fixes lane/vgpr/startPosn per element; 11.6.2 gives GLOBAL_LOAD_TR_B64/B128 load-and-transpose straight into operand registers
wmma_probed.measured: a naive 8-accumulator loop reached only 176 TOPS because it ignored the layout and hazard rules; rated dense int4 is 766 TOPS

operand_width_vs_density.rule: for a memory-bound quantised matmul no wider operand can win at T=1 (dp4a 8 bits, fp8 8, iu4 4, fp16 16 against 2 packed); at batch T>=64 the weight read is amortised and compute binds instead, so matrix cores win

context_budget.rule: context tokens = free_bytes / per_token_bytes, so on this model 1 GB of device memory is about 30000 tokens and the whole context question reduces to which byte is a weight, which is a scratch buffer and which is K/V
context_budget.operand_expansion_cost: widening the packed weights to 4-bit in device memory would cost about 6.8 GB, i.e. roughly 193000 tokens of context, which is larger than the entire context currently in use, while the same widening done in registers costs no device memory at all
context_budget.sharding: splitting weights and K/V over two devices halves both per-device, so it raises the per-device context by roughly 2.5x and also halves the bytes each device must read per token
